text: Targeted and Non-Targeted Analysis Reveal the Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substance (PFAS) Profiles in Hudson Bay Polar Bears Ecotoxicology and Wildlife Health Division, Environment & Climate Change Canada, National Wildlife Research Centre, Carleton University, Ottawa, ON, K1A 0H3, Canada Liver samples from n=20 (adult male) SHB (Sanikiluaq) and WHB (Rankin Inlet, Whale Cove and Arviat) bears sampled in 2019-2020 Development of a combined method to determine targeted, legacy and alternative PFAS as well as PFAS NTA with application for PFAS profiling in the liver of Hudson Bay polar bears Table 1: PFAS concentrations (ng/g wet weight) in polar bear liver samples from Hudson Bay Figure 1: An extracted ion chromatogram of linear and branched PFOS (m/z 498.9302) isomers in a representative sample of a polar bear liver samples We thank Amelie Roberto-Charron and the Nunavut Department of Environment and participating Nunavut HTOs (Arviat, Rankin Inlet, Whale Cove and Sanikiluaq). We thank laboratory technicians and field staff at NDE and ECCC (NWRC, David Blair) for processing sub-samples. Collections were made during subsistence harvests by Inuit hunters in late 2019 and early 2020, and according to valid 2019 and 2020 Nunavut Wildlife Research Permits. Financial support was provided by the NCP (CIRNAC; to R.J.L.).
